chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about clay. He replied, 'Eating clay is unlawful, like the carcass, blood, and flesh of a swine, except for the clay of the grave of al-Husayn, for verily it contains a cure from every disease and safety from every fear.'

key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْن: Clay of the grave of Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating clay in Shia Islam and what is the exception for the clay of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the general prohibition of eating clay by comparing it to major impurities like carrion and blood, yet elevates the clay of Imam al-Husayn’s grave as a unique spiritual and physical remedy. This exception highlights the concept of *shifa* (healing) and *amn* (security) inherent in the progeny of the Prophet, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory and curative power of the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration underscores how specific elements associated with the Imams transcend general rulings to offer divine mercy.
